habitat: Pairs in woodland, riparian woodland and bushveld.
summary: A fairly common summer resident. Pied, with a crest and a heavily streaked throat and breast, and larger than the white morph of Jacobin Cuckoo. The sexes are alike. The call is a flute-like peeeoo, six to eight times, then a rapid wherwher about twenty times. It parasitises babblers. Months were left unset. The Kemp code VB was left unchanged.

similar.note: The white morph of Jacobin Cuckoo has clear white underparts. Levaillant’s Cuckoo is larger and heavily streaked on the throat and breast.

population.notes: Kemp et al. 2001 order-of-magnitude threshold 2^14=16384 mature individuals (visiting breeder); paper interval half–double → 8192–32768.

sources.title: Kemp A.C., Herholdt J.J., Whyte I. & Harrison J. (2001). Birds of the two largest national parks in South Africa: a method to generate estimates of population size for all species and assess their conservation ecology. S. Afr. J. Sci. 97: 393–403.

head.pattern: Crested head. Throat and breast heavily streaked.

Streaked throat and breast, and a crest.
Black upper parts and a crest. The streaking is on the throat and breast.

Streaked throat and breast. The belly was included in the pied underparts.

calls.description: A flute-like peeeoo peeeoo, six to eight times, then a rapid wherwher about twenty times. Grade A from Ouagadougou. The catalogue types it as song and the filename says lev-cuckoo. No grade A recording from southern Africa was in the set.
